notes: Open Power System Data. 2020. Data Package Household Data. Version 2020-04-15. https://data.open-power-system-data.org/household_data/2020-04-15/. Primary data from the CoSSMic project (Konstanz, Germany). CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. The load of each site is reconstructed as grid import plus solar; values were differenced from cumulative meter readings.
Real public measurements, not MIZAN's own data. The load of each site is reconstructed as grid import plus solar; the no-export gate checks that neither site ever exported.
Costs are in RASID's illustrative tariff units, scaled to each site's size; no currency follows from them. The battery is hypothetical: neither site has one in this data.
Intervals come from a moving-block bootstrap of 7 target days whose blocks never span a gap between runs; many intervals are reported and none is adjusted for multiple comparisons.

Pooled results are unit-free and weight each site equally: cost differences divided by the site's mean daily no-battery cost, accuracy differences by the site's mean load, both held fixed over all target days.

provenance.note: HEAD and tracked-file state when the run started

scenario_rule: Five equally weighted scenarios (weight 0.2 each) from the forecaster's quantiles at levels 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 and 0.9, numbered j = 0 to 4: scenario j pairs load quantile path j with solar quantile path 4 − j, so high load meets low solar. Before pairing, each hour's quantiles are sorted across levels (monotone rearrangement) and solar values below zero are clipped at zero (counted in pv_values_clipped). Load quantiles are not clipped: a negative load value stops the run at the planner's input check. The chronos and chronos_risk_neutral policies are the candidate (risk weight 0.35) and candidate_risk_neutral problems with only these weights and scenarios replaced; the ridge policies keep their four reduced residual scenarios as shipped.

settings.analysis: RASID on real load: two business sites from the Open Power System Data household package
settings.currency: none: every cost is in RASID's illustrative tariff units

gate.generated_chronos: against the Chronos side of reports/hf/rasid.json: chronos_mae_kw, chronos_mean_pinball, chronos_truncated_crps and chronos_coverage_80_load within 1e-9; chronos and chronos_risk_neutral totals within 1e-6 relative; plan counts exact
gate.generated_ridge: hf_evaluation.rasid_gate against reports/evaluation/rasid.json: MAE within 1e-9 kW, candidate totals within 5e-4 relative, other totals within 1e-6 relative, plan counts exact

rules.10_bootstrap_and_pooling: Blocks of 7 consecutive target days inside one run, a shorter run as one block; draws pick blocks uniformly, concatenate and truncate to the site's day count; 4000 draws, seed 2026. Pooled: unit-free (cost differences / the site's mean daily no-battery cost, MAE / the site's mean load, share as is), each site weighted equally, sites resampled independently, normalisers fixed from all target days.
rules.11_readings: Resolved when the 95% interval excludes zero; an interval touching zero is not resolved; no multiplicity adjustment.
rules.12_refusals: No plan within the planner's limit, a plan the verifier rejects, or a refused planner input: the day is dropped for every policy and forecaster, recorded by cause and policy, and the run ends there.
rules.1_hourly_energy: Each row holds the cumulative reading at the end of the hour it is labelled with. The energy of hour t is reading(t) - reading(t - 1h); it is missing when either row is absent or the rows are not exactly one hour apart, when a difference is below -1e-9 kWh, or when a used column is named in `interpolated` at t or at t - 1h.
rules.2_load: Solar is the sum of the site's two solar columns; load is grid import plus solar (reconstructed).
rules.3_clean_day: A local day (Europe/Berlin) is clean when every one of its hours has all three energies, its grid import is not identical hour by hour to the previous local day's, and its grid import has no run of four or more identical non-zero hourly values; energies compared after rounding to 1e-6 kWh. A clean hour is an hour of a clean day.
rules.4_no_export_gate: Over clean hours, any hour with solar above 0.2 x the 99th-percentile solar while grid import is below 0.02 x the median load stops the run before anything is forecast.
rules.5_target_day: A clean day of 24 hours whose 7 previous local days are clean and which the ridge forecaster accepts; a ridge refusal is counted by cause and the day is not a target. Target days form runs of consecutive days.
rules.6_forecast_inputs: History: every clean hour before the origin (local midnight) within 300 days, known one hour after it starts. Ridge: rasid.forecast.forecast(rows, origin, grid, 4) over the 24 local hours; seasonal baseline: its seasonal_naive path; Chronos: models.chronos_forecaster on the contiguous clean hours ending at the hour before the origin, at most 2048, under hf_evaluation.SCENARIO_RULE.
rules.7_battery_and_tariff: examples.settings(24) with capacity, power, initial and terminal charge times s = mean load over the site's first 28 clean days / the mean load of examples.electricity(102); grid limit 2 x the site's largest clean hourly load; prices, risk 0.35, beta 0.90, efficiencies and cycles unchanged; time-of-use prices by local hour, as shipped.
rules.8_carried_state: Each policy carries its battery charge and month-to-date peak; the peak resets at each local month's start; at the start of each run both reset to the initial charge (no_battery at 0) and a peak of 0.
rules.9_measures: Per site: load MAE of ridge, baseline and Chronos median; pinball loss and truncated CRPS on 0.1, 0.5, 0.9; 80% coverage; decision_summary per policy; share of achievable battery value per policy with an interval; paired daily cost differences for the comparisons below; paired MAE differences.
